answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on shared work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated contributions. One attacker may create a thousand names, but each must lock real value and risk losing it; splitting identities does not multiply the attacker’s budget. A harbor-style review queue can sample claims, while shale and comet serve as ordinary project labels, not trusted credentials. This raises the cost of Sybil influence without pretending to prove one human per account.
